title: Connect to RDS from C#
description: Connect an ASP.NET Core app to RDS using EF Core, Dapper, or ADO.NET.

data.text: Connecting to RDS from C# is the same as connecting to any SQL Server or PostgreSQL database. The main difference is that the connection string comes from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store rather than appsettings.json.

data.title: Use RDS with EF Core in Program.cs
data.content: Pull the connection string from configuration loaded by Secrets Manager.

data.text: RDS instances are not publicly accessible by default. You must create a security group rule to allow your app's IP or VPC to reach the database.

data.title: Allow access from Elastic Beanstalk
data.content: Use the AWS CLI to create a security group rule.
data.code:
$vpcId = aws elasticbeanstalk describe-environment-resources --environment-name aspnet-aws-env --query EnvironmentResources.EnvironmentResources.VpcId --output text
$sgId = aws rds describe-db-instances --db-instance-identifier aspnet-db --query 'DBInstances[0].VpcSecurityGroups[0].VpcSecurityGroupId' --output text

aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id $sgId --protocol tcp --port 1433 --source-group $vpcId

data.text: In development, use `dotnet ef database update` to apply migrations. In production, use `context.Database.Migrate()` or a deployment script.

data.title: Auto-apply migrations at startup
data.content: Apply pending migrations automatically when the app starts.

data.title: Build a posts API with EF Core and RDS
data.description: Create a minimal API that stores posts in RDS using EF Core.
steps: Create an RDS SQL Server or PostgreSQL instance
Add a connection string from Secrets Manager
Create the initial migration and apply it
data.expectedOutcome: You can create and list posts through HTTP endpoints backed by RDS.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `UseSqlServer` for SQL Server or `UseNpgsql` for PostgreSQL
Store connection strings in Secrets Manager or Parameter Store
Configure security groups to allow app-to-database traffic
Use `Migrate()` in development; prefer controlled migrations in production
data.takeaway: RDS and EF Core integrate cleanly when you separate connection configuration, security groups, and migration strategy.
